question.leadin: The Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa paved the way for successful later sieges of Cordoba and Seville in this conflict.
question.text: Name this religious conflict between Christian states and Muslim states in the Iberian Peninsula, which is named for the reacquisition of traditionally Christian lands.
question.clue: During this period, a coalition of Christian knights joined together to defeat Muhammad al-Nasir at the Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa.

swap.leadin: Despite underestimating the Earth's circumference by a factor of 5, his trip was still a success.
swap.text: Name this Italian explorer working for Spain, who landed in America on October 12, 1492.
swap.clue: His rivals included a subordinate on his first trip, Martin Pinzon, as well as Francisco de Babadilla who arrested him and his brothers Bartholemew and Diego for mismanagement of the newly founded La Isabela.

question.leadin: This group was commanded by the Duke of Medina Sidonia after its initially designated leader, Alvaro de Bazan, died.
question.text: Name this massive naval fleet whose intended invasion of England failed.
question.answerHtml: Spanish Armada [accept Grande y Felicisima Armada or Invincible Armada or Armada Invencible]
question.clue: The plan was for this force to join with one under Alessandro Farnese, but before that could happen, it participated in its first engagement off Eddystone.

swap.text: Merged with the Carlists by Franco, this Spanish fascist movement was founded by Jose Antonio Primo de Rivera.
swap.clue: Two leaders of this party were buried within the Santa Cruz Basilica at the Valley of the Fallen.

question.text: At the Battle of Sagrajas, El Cid commanded a force of these people. Charles Martel defeated these people at the Battle of Tours.
question.clue: This umbrella term used to describe Arab and North-African Muslims who controlled parts of Southern Europe from Spain to Sicily in the Medieval period.

swap.text: This Dominican friar was the first Grand Inquisitor, becoming infamous for his zeal and cruelty.
swap.clue: This confessor of Isabella also led the the Spanish Inquisition as the Grand Inquisitor.

question.text: Unsurprisingly, Salazar was a big fan of this longtime dictator of Spain, who ruled from 1939 to 1975. His party was known as the Falange, and he was supported by the Carlists.
question.clue: This leader created an air bridge using Junker-52s to deploy his Army of Africa in a coup against Manuel Azana's Popular Front.

swap.text: The captains of all five ships were killed before the completion of the Magellan Expedition. This man managed to complete the circumnavigation after taking over as captain of the Victoria.
swap.clue: This man was promoted to lead one expedition after his predecessor was (+) killed at the Battle of Mactan.

question.text: Juana was the second daughter of this queen of Castile. Her marriage to Ferdinand of Aragon united the Spanish nation.
question.clue: With the assistance of Tomas de Torquemada, this daughter of John II issued the Alhambra Decree, which expelled all of the Jews from her country.

swap.leadin: A person of this ethnicity, Alonso de Ercilla ("air-SEE-yah"), wrote an epic poem about the conquest of Chile.
swap.text: Give this ethnicity of many conquerors and settlers of the New World, some of whom formed the Gipuzkoan ("geez-poo-KOH-ahn") Company in Venezuela.
swap.clue: Speakers of this language owned and operated the Royal Gipuzkoan Company.

question.text: This grandson of Alfonso XIII officially ended the Spanish monarchy's right to name Roman Catholic bishops in 1976. He also teased the conservative King of Belgium while signing off on legalizing gay marriage in Spain in 2005.
question.answerHtml: King Juan Carlos I [or Juan Carlos Alfonso Víctor María de Borbón y Borbón-Dos Sicilias]
question.clue: A June 2014 decision by this man led to a rise in rank for former television anchor Letizia Ortiz.

swap.text: Cod was also essential for this ethnic group, whose members dominated the whaling industry from settlements by the Ebro. In 1615, Icelandic sailors killed a group of them in the so-called "Slaying of the Spaniards."
swap.clue: Whalers of this ethnicity were killed in Iceland in 1615 after conflict over stolen fish.

question.text: Searching for the land of Bimini, this guy spent his career surveying Florida in the early 1500s supposedly in pursuit of the Fountain of Youth.
question.clue: Rumors of gold led him to establish the colony of Caparra, the first European settlement in Puerto Rico.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Confederacion Nacional del Trabajo ("trah-BAH-hoh"), or CNT.
swap.text: The CNT was founded following a 1910 workers' congress in this city. A 1909 general strike resulted in the "Tragic Week" in this capital of Catalonia.
swap.clue: A rebellion in this city erupted on July 19, 1936 when news of a coup launched by the military against the government of Manuel Azana reached it, with the result that the rebels captured the San Andres and Atarazanas barracks.

question.text: This first name was held both by a "Great" king of Pamplona and his three grandsons, who name a 1060s conflict in which Castile reconquered Alava. A later king with this name was the father of Berengaria of Navarre, who married Richard I of England.
question.clue: This name of several kings of Navarre and Castille. Another king with this name turned a 1212 battle with an uphill charge that forced Muhammad al-Nasir to retreat.

swap.text: Along with their brother Leander, this bishop and patron saint of the internet was instrumental in eliminating Arianism from the Visigothic kingdom, and also found time to compile their encyclopaedic Etymologiae.
swap.clue: This man who was described by Charles Montalembert as "the last scholar of the ancient world." His most famous work was a twenty-volume encyclopedia called Etymologiae.

question.text: As an homage to Blanche, Louis IX gifted a moralizing Bible completed in this city to her nephew, Ferdinand III. A medieval "school of translators" in this Castilian city was instrumental in preserving Arabic scientific texts.
question.answerHtml: Toledo [accept Toledo School of Translators or Escuela de Traductores de Toledo; accept Toledo Bible or Bible of Toledo]
question.clue: The third council in this city confirmed Reccared's decision to convert from Arianism to Catholicism.

swap.leadin: The GAL, or Antiterrorist Liberation Groups, targeted this organization in the Monbar Hotel attack.
swap.text: The newspaper The World exposed a PSOE leader's involvement in death squads targeting what organization? This organization's symbol was an axe with a snake around it, and it had the motto "Keep up in both."
swap.answerHtml: ETA [or Euskadi Ta Askatasuna or Basque Homeland and Liberty or Basque Country and Freedom; prompt on Basque separatists]
swap.clue: Members of this organization were prosecuted in the Burgos trials.

question.leadin: They posed the last obstacle of the Reconquista. FTPE.
question.text: After the Almohads were crushed in the Battle of Navas de Tolosa, this Moorish dynasty founded by Muhammed I al-Ghalib was the last major Muslim dynasty in Spain.

swap.leadin: The Onacino and Gamboino clans fought during this conflict.
swap.text: Name this conflict in medieval Spain between landowners called juanchos in which many dorretxeak were built.
swap.answerHtml: The War of the Bands [accept Guerra de los Bandos; accept Bando Gerrak]
